Looking at the testimonies, Kay says in testimony 4: "Umm... That's right, someone was walking towards me from the other side of that stand." The "stand" here probably refers to the candy stand mentioned in the Bigg Building Pamphlet (evidence 7). The pamphlet says the candy stand is on the right-most edge of the viewing platform.

Now, looking at evidence 8, which is Kay's recollections. She remembers a person coming from beyond the concession stand and pushing her off the building. Wait, the "concession stand" here might be the same as the candy stand mentioned in the pamphlet. So if the person came from beyond the candy stand, that would be to the right of the candy stand since it's on the right edge. But in testimony 4, Kay says someone was coming from the other side of the stand. The other side would be the left side relative to the stand. But if the stand is on the right-most edge, there's no left side beyond it. So if someone came from beyond the candy stand, they'd have to be on the right, but the other side of the stand (from where Kay was) would be the left. That might create a contradiction in the direction of where the person came from.

Applying the spatial reasoning rules: The Bigg Building Pamphlet (evidence 7) describes the layout. The candy stand is on the right-most edge. So if someone is beyond the candy stand (evidence 8), they can't be on the left side (testimony 4) because the candy stand is already at the right edge. So the direction from which the person approached contradicts between the evidence and testimony. The rules here might not directly apply because they involve coverage or positioning, but the contradiction is about the spatial location relative to the stand. 

Therefore, evidence 8 (Kay's recollections) and testimony 4 (her statement about the other side of the stand) contradict each other spatially.
